title: [YSQL] Wrong offset when preparing fast path update
body:
### Description

Reproducer:
```
yugabyte=# create table orders2 (order_row_id uuid,  total_executed_qty numeric, order_status_cd character varying(1), primary key (order_row_id));
CREATE TABLE
yugabyte=# update orders2 set TOTAL_EXECUTED_QTY=TOTAL_EXECUTED_QTY+1, ORDER_STATUS_CD='B'  where order_row_id='5a5c3d42-638a-465a-8f49-8541ebb35e6c';
ERROR:  invalid memory alloc request size 18446744073709551613
```

The fast path update plan looks like this:
```
yugabyte=# explain verbose update orders2 set TOTAL_EXECUTED_QTY=TOTAL_EXECUTED_QTY+1, ORDER_STATUS_CD='B'  where order_row_id='5a5c3d42-638a-465a-8f49-8541ebb35e6c';
                                         QUERY PLAN                                         
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Update on public.orders2  (cost=0.00..4.12 rows=1 width=88)
   ->  Result  (cost=0.00..4.12 rows=1 width=88)
         Output: '5a5c3d42-638a-465a-8f49-8541ebb35e6c'::uuid, 0, 'B'::character varying(1)
(3 rows)
```
The 0 value in the Result's output is a placeholder for the expression we pushdown. The data type for the placeholder is int4, this type is used by Result to construct the tuple. However, when we construct the update request, we use tuple descriptor from the target table which is numeric type in our example above, so the third attribute is looked for at incorrect offset.

~~This issue is fixed in master by https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/commit/32007863a784e3d228a4e51709357f634ad12dc2, but this change is too big to backport. We need a smaller fix for that issue to backport to all supported versions.~~

Same issue exists in master but is harder to hit. Here is a test case:
```
yugabyte=# set yb_enable_expression_pushdown to true;
SET
yugabyte=# create table orders1(id uuid primary key, quantity numeric, status char(1));
CREATE TABLE
yugabyte=# create table orders2(id uuid primary key, quantity numeric, status char(1));
CREATE TABLE
yugabyte=# create function status2(uuid) returns char(1) language sql as $$ select status from orders2 where id=$1; $$;
CREATE FUNCTION
yugabyte=# insert into orders2 values('5a5c3d42-638a-465a-8f49-8541ebb35e6c', 1, 'A');
INSERT 0 1
yugabyte=# update orders1 set quantity=quantity+1, status=status2('5a5c3d42-638a-465a-8f49-8541ebb35e6c') where id='5a5c3d42-638a-465a-8f49-8541ebb35e6c';
ERROR:  invalid memory alloc request size 18446744073709551613
```
